edits.content:
## Compare the Full Logical Claims

### Track quantifier scope and dependencies
Before evaluating an option, write down who chooses each object and what it may depend on. For example, distinguish a single witness required to work for every parameter from a witness chosen separately for each parameter; likewise distinguish a constant that may depend on \(\varepsilon\) from one uniform in \(\varepsilon\). Preserve differences such as “for every \(N\)” versus “for all sufficiently large \(N\).”

### Check every rider and compare by implication
Split compound options into their clauses. An extra structural requirement, a claim that a result holds after dropping a hypothesis, or a more specific output guarantee must be verified separately; the main conclusion alone does not establish it. Compare claims by logical implication or set containment, not by phrasing. In particular, containment in a finitely generated subalgebra adds a restriction beyond containment in a larger algebra, while restricting the permitted generators makes an algebra-containment claim stronger.

### Verify existential and algorithmic guarantees
For an existential claim, give a witness satisfying all the stated conditions and calculate the quantity being bounded or compared. Check the threshold and relevant boundary cases rather than relying on a plausible construction. For algorithmic claims, compare the full input domain, required outputs or failure reports, and running-time bound; a faster bound on a restricted case is not the same guarantee as that bound on all cases.
